note: Hand-curated, sourced entries. A consensus national toss-up. Ballotpedia lists three qualified unaffiliated/independent general-election candidates (Alcorn, Rich, Evans), not curated here.

ME-senate.statusNote: Sen. Susan Collins (R), Senate Appropriations chair, faces former state Senate President Troy Jackson (D). Graham Platner won the June 9 Democratic primary with 72% but withdrew on July 10; the Maine Democratic Party nominated Jackson on July 25 and the Secretary of State lists him as the replacement candidate. Rated a toss-up by the Cook Political Report.

ME-house-1.statusNote: Rep. Chellie Pingree (D), unopposed in the June 9, 2026 primary, faces Republican Ron Russell, a retired Army Special Forces officer. Maine runs both the primary and the general with ranked choice voting.

sources.label: The Green Papers: Maine 2026 general election candidates

ME-house-2.statusNote: Open seat: Rep. Jared Golden (D) is not seeking reelection. State Auditor Matt Dunlap (D) won the June 9, 2026 primary in a ranked choice runoff, 52.5 to 47.5 over Joe Baldacci, and faces former Gov. Paul LePage (R). Maine runs both the primary and the general with ranked choice voting.

candidates.name: Susan Collins
candidates.now: U.S. Senator; Chair, Senate Appropriations Committee
candidates.background: U.S. Senator since 1997, seeking a sixth term; chairs the Appropriations Committee and holds the longest perfect attendance streak in Senate history. From a sixth-generation Caribou lumber family. Repeatedly ranked the Senate's most bipartisan member; voted to convict President Trump in the 2021 impeachment trial.
priorities: Health care: Alzheimer's, diabetes, rural access

cost.label: Record: champions federal home-heating assistance; secured $4B in LIHEAP funding and pressed for its release (Senate office)

health.label: One of the Republican votes that blocked repealing the ACA without replacement in 2017; co-sponsored insulin and drug-price bills (Wikipedia)

housing.label: Record: directs federal affordable-housing funding to Maine as an appropriator (Senate office)

immigration.label: Voted for the 2013 comprehensive reform with a citizenship path; opposed family separation and the 2017 travel ban (Wikipedia)

taxes.label: Voted for the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act after securing SALT and medical-expense amendments (Senate office)

climate.label: Backs offshore wind expansion; co-authored a 30% offshore-wind investment tax credit (Senate office)

education.label: Voted against Betsy DeVos for Education Secretary, citing commitment to public and rural schools (Senate office)

repro.label: Self-identified pro-choice: opposed 20-week bans and Planned Parenthood defunding, but voted to confirm Justice Kavanaugh (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: Mixed: backs Electoral Count Act reform to stop Congress overriding state election results, but joined the GOP in blocking the Freedom to Vote: John R. Lewis Act in Jan 2022, calling it 'a federal takeover of state elections' (Maine Public)

safety.label: Voted yes on the First Step Act of 2018, the 87-12 sentencing-reform and prison-reentry law (Senate roll call 271)

controversies.label: Her Kavanaugh vote, cast after predicting he would not overturn Roe, was contradicted by the Dobbs decision (Wikipedia)

candidates.name: Graham Platner
candidates.background: Oyster farmer, Marine Corps and Army National Guard veteran (Iraq and Afghanistan), and political newcomer endorsed by Bernie Sanders. Won the June Democratic primary over Gov. Janet Mills, who had suspended her campaign in April. His campaign rejects PAC money and reported a $4.1M first-quarter 2026 haul, largely from working people.
priorities: Get billionaire money out of politics

cost.label: Raise the federal minimum wage and index it to inflation; 'cost-of-living tax cut' for working people (campaign platform)

health.label: Medicare for All, replacing for-profit insurance; Medicare drug-price negotiation (campaign platform)

housing.label: Restore federal housing investment, expand VA home loans, ban hedge funds from buying homes (campaign platform)

immigration.label: Opposes mass deportation; reform pairing strong border security with a path to citizenship (campaign platform)

taxes.label: Billionaire minimum tax; lift the Social Security payroll-tax cap (campaign platform)

climate.label: Urgent climate action; defend and strengthen Clean Air and Clean Water Act enforcement (campaign platform)

education.label: Opposes private-school vouchers; federal investment so every public district is adequately funded (campaign platform)

safety.label: Legalize cannabis with clemency for drug-war convictions; invest revenue in addiction treatment and prevention (campaign platform)

repro.label: Strong federal statutory guarantee of the right to choose (campaign platform)

controversies.label: A 2007 tattoo compared to the Nazi Totenkopf ('I never once thought about it in that context'), covered up once flagged, and offensive Reddit posts he admits were angry and crude, citing post-infantry trauma (WGME)

candidates.name: Troy Jackson
candidates.background: Fifth-generation logger from Allagash in Aroostook County who served 20 years in the Maine Legislature, including six years as Senate President from 2018 to 2024. Finished third in the 2026 Democratic primary for governor, then was chosen by the Maine Democratic Party on July 25, 2026 to replace Graham Platner as the Senate nominee after Platner withdrew July 10 amid controversy over past social media posts and a tattoo. A longtime labor and Bernie Sanders ally, he has drawn union endorsements, including the Association of Flight Attendants, and the League of Conservation Voters Action Fund's backing.
priorities: Medicare for All and lower prescription drug costs
Tax billionaires and corporations, cut taxes for working people

cost.label: As a state senator campaigning for a minimum wage referendum: '$15,600 a year is what you get for a 40-hour workweek in Maine if you're working minimum wage, and that is not enough for anyone' (Maine Beacon)

health.label: Campaign priority: 'Pass Medicare for all and lower the cost of prescription drugs' (Jackson campaign)

immigration.label: Campaign priority: 'Dismantle and abolish ICE' (Jackson campaign)

taxes.label: Campaign priority: 'Tax the billionaires and make sure greedy corporations pay their fair share' (Jackson campaign)

climate.label: Pledged to 'fight for clean energy investments that lower costs, create union jobs here at home, and preserve Maine's natural resources for our kids and grandkids', earning a League of Conservation Voters Action Fund endorsement (Jackson campaign)

education.label: Campaign bio: as Senate President he 'championed and passed universal school meals' (Jackson campaign)

repro.label: Campaign priority: 'Pass a federal right to abortion' (Jackson campaign)

democracy.label: Campaign priority: 'Protect the right to vote and organize for every American' (Jackson campaign)

nullNotes.housing: Campaign priorities and about pages, Maine Public's Senate-nomination coverage, and Ballotpedia contain no housing-specific policy beyond a general reference to Mainers 'getting crushed by the cost of health care, housing, groceries and heat', which names a hardship rather than a stance on building, zoning, or tenant protections (checked Aug 31, 2026)
nullNotes.safety: Campaign priorities, news pages, and available news coverage contain no policing or sentencing position; his legislative committee record (Agriculture, Labor, Energy) does not touch criminal justice (checked Aug 31, 2026)

candidates.name: Chellie M Pingree
candidates.now: U.S. Representative for Maine's 1st District since 2009
candidates.background: Organic farmer and former Maine Senate majority leader who has represented the 1st District since 2009. A senior member of the House Appropriations Committee, she was unopposed in the June 9, 2026 Democratic primary.

cost.label: Campaign platform: 'anyone who works hard at a full time job is paid a livable wage', wages stagnant while CEOs get windfalls (Pingree campaign)

health.label: 'The time has come to pass Medicare for All. With a single-payer system, we can address unreasonable out-of-pocket costs' (Pingree campaign)

housing.label: 'Fought so strongly to fund' affordable housing projects, citing that nearly half of Maine tenants cannot afford rent (pingree.house.gov)

immigration.label: Voted no on the Laken Riley Act's expanded immigration detention mandates (House Clerk roll 23, Jan 22, 2025)

taxes.label: 'We need a tax code that asks the rich to pay their share, rather than giving them more massive tax breaks' (Pingree campaign); also voted no on the 2025 H.R. 1 tax law (House Clerk roll 190)

climate.label: 'Quickly transitioning our power and transportation systems from dirty fossil fuels to clean... renewable sources is critical'; opposes offshore oil drilling (Pingree campaign)

repro.label: 'We cannot compromise on a woman's absolute right to make decisions about her own health care'; committed to protecting Roe (Pingree campaign)

democracy.label: Voted no on the SAVE Act's documentary proof-of-citizenship requirement for voter registration (House Clerk roll 102, Apr 10, 2025)

nullNotes.education: campaign issues page speaks only to higher-education affordability and a generic 'world-class education'; no K-12 public-investment versus school-choice position documented there or on Ballotpedia (no Candidate Connection survey filed)
nullNotes.safety: campaign issues page addresses only gun safety, which does not map to this axis; no policing or sentencing approach documented

candidates.name: Ronald Charles Russell
candidates.now: Retired Army Special Forces officer and defense company founder
candidates.background: Maine native who served just over 30 years in the Army as an Airborne Ranger and Green Beret, then founded a defense contracting company he grew to more than 150 employees. Won the June 9, 2026 Republican primary to challenge Rep. Chellie Pingree.

cost.label: Says Washington policies are 'crushing Maine's middle class'; would lower fuel and grocery costs through tax reduction and deregulation (Russell campaign)

health.label: Would 'ensure that Medicaid is available to those who need it by eliminating the fraud, waste, and abuse', and would end coverage for undocumented immigrants (Maine Public)

immigration.label: 'Joe Biden's open border policies have failed America'; embraces legal immigration with vetting but calls border security the priority and wants the amnesty system reformed (Russell campaign)

taxes.label: Advocates making temporary tax relief permanent and work-linked credits 'instead of growing welfare programs' (Russell campaign)

climate.label: 'The most important thing we can do to strengthen our economy is to become energy independent'; says current technology cannot replace fossil fuels and opposes energy-source mandates (Russell campaign)

education.label: Backs 'reforms like school choice', a stronger parental voice, and says 'we can't just pour more money into a system that isn't improving' (Russell campaign)

safety.label: 'We must restore law and order'; violent criminals should serve full sentences, police need better pay and funding, calls defund-the-police 'dangerous' (Russell campaign)

repro.label: Answered no when asked whether he supports abortion rights in Maine Public's candidate profile lightning round (Maine Public)

democracy.label: 'Reforms such as voter ID are common-sense measures', while saying integrity can be ensured 'without depriving individuals of their right to vote' (Russell campaign)

nullNotes.housing: campaign site issue pages and the Maine Public profile contain no housing policy position

candidates.name: Matt Dunlap
candidates.now: Maine State Auditor, former longtime Secretary of State
candidates.background: Maine State Auditor and former four-plus-term Secretary of State from Old Town. Won the June 2026 Democratic primary for the open 2nd District seat in a ranked choice runoff, 52.5 to 47.5 over Joe Baldacci, after Rep. Jared Golden declined to seek reelection.
priorities: Lower healthcare costs through Medicare for All
Making billionaires and corporations pay their fair share

cost.label: Campaigns on universal childcare and taking on 'the powerful interests that have rigged our economy against working class Mainers' (Dunlap campaign)

health.label: 'Move toward a Medicare for All system that actually brings down healthcare costs for working families' (Maine Public)

housing.label: Mixed: backs removing construction barriers while also targeting private equity firms that buy homes and drive up prices (Maine Morning Star voter guide)

immigration.label: Calls recent ICE conduct in Maine 'indiscriminate and heavy-handed'; would cut ICE supplemental funding and impose oversight (Maine Morning Star voter guide)

taxes.label: Supports the Sanders-Khanna billionaire tax and busting the payroll tax cap so 'the wealthiest are paying their fair share' (Maine Morning Star voter guide; Maine Public)

climate.label: Would restore the Inflation Reduction Act's clean energy tax credits and invest in domestically produced renewable energy (Maine Public; Maine Morning Star voter guide)

repro.label: Answered yes when asked whether he supports abortion rights in Maine Public's lightning round (Maine Public)

democracy.label: Answered no on requiring photo ID to vote; as Secretary of State ran Maine's elections and defended their integrity (Maine Public)

nullNotes.education: campaign site, Maine Public profile, and Maine Morning Star voter guide contain no K-12 public-investment versus school-choice position
nullNotes.safety: campaign site, Maine Public profile, and Maine Morning Star voter guide contain no policing or sentencing position

sources.label: Maine Morning Star Democratic primary voter guide

candidates.name: Paul Lepage
candidates.background: Two-term Governor of Maine (2011 to 2019) and former Waterville mayor who grew up homeless in Lewiston before a business career. Lost the 2022 governor's race to Janet Mills and is now the Republican nominee for the open 2nd District seat, endorsed by the U.S. Chamber of Commerce.
priorities: Finish the border wall and end illegal immigration

cost.label: 'Lower taxes. Less red tape. More jobs for Maine families'; would 'eliminate wasteful spending which drove up inflation' (LePage campaign)

health.label: Vetoed five MaineCare expansion bills, refused to implement the 2017 voter-approved Medicaid expansion, and backs new Medicaid work requirements (Maine Morning Star)

immigration.label: 'Paul will fight to finish the wall, end illegal immigration, and restore law and order' (LePage campaign)

taxes.label: Campaign platform of lower taxes and eliminating wasteful spending (LePage campaign)

climate.label: As governor pushed to eliminate Maine's renewable portfolio standard, 'I'm against those that add costs to our electricity bills', and urged a shift to natural gas (NRCM)

education.label: Defended charter schools as governor, publicly opposing House Speaker Eves' hiring over his 'anti-charter school stance' (Ballotpedia)

safety.label: Vetoed expanded naloxone access as governor, saying 'the lack of consequences for serious drug use is having the opposite effect' (Ballotpedia)

repro.label: Mixed record: attended anti-abortion rallies and opposed MaineCare abortion funding as governor, but in 2022 said yes he would veto a 15-week abortion ban and had 'never, ever attempted to change' Maine's 1993 abortion law (Bangor Daily News)

democracy.label: Made a photo ID requirement a prominent campaign plank and repeatedly claimed fraud risk in larger Maine cities (Maine Public)

nullNotes.housing: 2026 campaign site and current race coverage contain no housing policy position
